                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to make your Express.js APIs 9x faster with Encore.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-09-10, last updated: 2025-10-10, [Read more](https://dev.to/encore/how-to-make-your-expressjs-apis-9x-faster-with-encorets-1ke2)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### 4.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Configure your tsconfig.json\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tsconfig.json\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'file in the root of your project, add the following:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"compilerOptions": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"paths": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"~encore/*": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"./encore.gen/*"\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When Encore.ts is parsing your code it will specifically look for\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'~encore/*\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'imports.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import {api, Query} from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Dynamic path parameter :name\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const dynamicPathParamExample = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{expose: true, method: "GET", path: "/hello/:name"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async ({name}: { name: string }): Promise<{ message: string }> => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import {api} from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import {anotherService} from "~encore/clients";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const microserviceCommunication = api(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{expose: true, method: "GET", path: "/call"},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async (): Promise<{ message: string }> => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Calling the foo endpoint in anotherService\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const fooResponse = await anotherService.foo();'[39m

                      [32m'└── api.ts # API endpoints\n'[39m +

                      [32m'}\n'[39m +

                      [32m"The id is your app's unique identifier.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'export default new Service("my-service");\n'[39m +

                      [32m'return { message: "Hello, World!"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To require authentication for an API endpoint, add `auth: true` to the API options.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"With this option, Encore will first call the authentication handler you've defined to validate the authentication of incoming requests.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"Setting `auth: true` can also be useful for internal APIs that aren't exposed to the internet.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'In that case, it means that the internal caller must have valid authentication data associated with its request.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Finally, even if an API endpoint does not specify `auth: true`, it will still receive any authentication data that was provided.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'import { api } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +

                      [32m'interface PingParams {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: string;\n'[39m +

                      [32m'// PingResponse is the response data for the Ping endpoint.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface PingResponse {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'message: string;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// hello is an API endpoint that responds with a simple response.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Now protect any endpoint with `auth: true`.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Custom Middleware in Encore.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-12-09, last updated: 2026-06-20, [Read more](https://encore.dev/blog/custom-middleware)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore.ts makes it simple to create middleware by letting you attach middleware functions to specific services through the service definitions configuration.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Middleware can be configured with a `target` option to specify which API endpoints it applies to, such as those requiring authentication.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Example\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The simplest way to create a middleware is to use the `middleware` helper in `encore.dev/api`,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'here is an example of a middleware that will run for endpoints that require auth:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { middleware } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default new Service("myService", {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'middlewares: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'middleware({ target: { auth: true } }, async (req, next) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// do something before the api handler\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const resp = await next(req);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// do something after the api handler\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return resp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },

                      [32m'In this case it only\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Adding authentication to APIs to auth users\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-03, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/ts/develop/auth)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When an API is defined with `auth: true`, you must define an authentication handler\n'[39m +
                      [32m'in your application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The authentication handler is responsible for inspecting incoming\n'[39m +
                      [32m'requests to determine what user is authenticated (if any), and computing any other associated\n'[39m +
                      [32m'authentication information.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The authentication handler is defined similarly to API endpoints, using the `authHandler`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function imported from `encore.dev/auth`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Like API endpoints, the authentication handler defines what request information it's interested in,\n"[39m +
                      [32m'in the form of HTTP headers, query strings, or cookies.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { authHandler } from "encore.dev/auth";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const auth = authHandler<AuthParams, AuthData>(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async (params) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return {userID: "my-user-id"};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m')\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Define the API Gateway that will execute the auth handler:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const gateway = new Gateway({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'authHandler: auth,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'With this in place, Encore will provision an API Gateway that will process\n'[39m +
                      [32m'incoming requests to your application, and whenever a request contains\n'[39m +
                      [32m'an `Authorization` header it will first call the authentication handler to\n'[39m +
                      [32m'resolve information about the user.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# BetterAuth with Encore.ts - Complete Backend Guide\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-11-12, last updated: 2026-07-01, [Read more](https://encore.dev/blog/betterauth-tutorial)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Rather than wrapping each one in a separate Encore endpoint, you can mount the entire Better Auth handler on a single catch-all route using `toNodeHandler` from `better-auth/node`:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore has a built-in auth handler pattern that lets you validate incoming requests in one place.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You define a handler function that extracts and validates credentials, and Encore REDACTEDmatically runs it before any endpoint marked with `auth: true`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The data you return from the handler becomes available to the endpoint via `getAuthData()`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const handler = authHandler<AuthParams, AuthData>(async (params) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Forward the relevant headers to Better Auth for validation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// This supports both cookie-based (browser) and token-based (API) auth.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const headers = new Headers();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const session = await auth.api.getSession({ headers });\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'throw APIError.unauthenticated("invalid session");\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return { userID: session.user.id };\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// The gateway applies the auth handler to all incoming requests.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const gateway = new Gateway({ authHandler: handler });\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Encore can generate a type-safe TypeScript client that matches your backend API, so your frontend stays in sync without any manual work:'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# encore-auth - Implement authentication with auth handlers and ga\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-02-04, last updated: 2026-03-29, [Read more](https://skill4agent.com/en/skill/encoredev-skills/encore-auth)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 1.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Create an Auth Handler\n'[39m +
                      [32m'typescript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// auth.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { Header, Gateway } from "encore.dev/api";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { authHandler } from "encore.dev/auth";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Define what the auth handler receives\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface AuthParams {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'authorization: Header<"Authorization">;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Define what authenticated requests will have access to\n'[39m +
                      [32m'interface AuthData {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'userID: string;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'email: string;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'role: "admin" | "user";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const auth = authHandler<AuthParams, AuthData>(\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async (params) => {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Validate the token (example with JWT)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const token = params.authorization.replace("Bearer ", "");\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const payload = await verifyToken(token);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (!payload) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'throw APIError.unauthenticated("invalid token");\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'userID: payload.sub,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'email: payload.email,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'role: payload.role,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m');\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Register the auth handler with a Gateway\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export const gateway = new Gateway({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'authHandler: auth,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When users ask you to perform tasks, check if any of the available skills below can help complete the task more effectively. Skills provide specialized capabilities and domain knowledge.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'- NEVER just announce or mention a skill in your text response without actually calling this tool (except for general skill listing requests)\n'[39m +
